A total of 16 teams competed in the tournament. [[Sporting Cristal]] won its 13th first division title, completing a string of 3 consecutive titles starting in 1994. The feat is known as a ''tricampeonato'' and was previously accomplished only by [[Alianza Lima]].[https://clubsportingcristal.pe/historia/19-historia/campeones/114-campeon-1996 Sporting Cristal campeón 1996][https://elbocon.pe/futbol-peruano/descentralizado/sporting-cristal-un-dia-como-hoy-los-celestes-fueron-tricampeones-134168/ Sporting Cristal: Un día como hoy los celestes fueron tricampeones][https://libero.pe/futbol-peruano/2012-08-19-lo-que-tu-viejo-no-te-conto-el-tri-de-sporting-cristal-de-1996-fue-una-locura Lo que tu viejo no te contó: El “Tri” de Sporting Cristal de 1996 fue una locura] ==Changes from 1995== *The tournament would be played like in 1994, where the champion was crowned after the first stage of the tournament and the second berth to the Copa Libertadores was determined by an end-of-season Liguilla featuring 4 teams. *Four teams were relegated instead of the customary two.
